text: Okay. The purpose of the meeting is to consider an application of a minor variance and it's on for 159 Old Orchard Road. And we'll let Forbes go ahead and do the presentation for the planner.

speaker: forbess
text: Thank you very much, Chair. Everybody has received a copy of my planning report and I'll go through and summarize my assessment, Chair, if I may. So the property is an existing lot of record. It fronts on the Rideau River and it is developed by a cottage. The property, the proposal is to redevelop the property with a new dwelling with a similar setback from the water that the existing development has. The existing development has a 20 meter setback from the water. The proposed new development will have a similar 20 meter setback. In addition to the reduction or request and reduction from the 30 meter to the 20 meters for the water setback, there's also a request to reduce the rear yard setback from 7.5 to 3.2 meters and to allow for an increase in the maximum lot coverage from 10% to 14%. The proposed or the existing dwelling on the property is about 68 square meters in size. The proposed new development's going to be 107 square meters in size, but that does include an attached garage. The applicant submitted, the application that was submitted by Zander Plan indicated that the lot is severely undersized making compliance with lot coverage and yard setbacks not possible. And they also noted that part of the property is zoned floodplain as well associated with the Rideau River. The property is in the settlement area of Andrewsville and as such, it's an appropriate location for development that's being proposed. I have identified the limited service residential zone provisions in my report. I'm not going to go through those. And also I highlighted that section 327 of the bylaw has the 30 meter water setback. At the time of the writing of my report chair, there were no comments of concern or objection. And I did do a fairly thorough assessment of the proposed development against the four tests set out in the planning act. The first test is does this maintain the intent and purpose of the official plan? Now, clearly this is an area where development is to be directed towards being within the Hamlet and it would be deemed as a result, this is in keeping with the official plan and the application has been deemed to conform with the township's official plan. In terms of the bylaw, there are a number of elements that are being asked to be reduced. The 30 meter setback reflects is the standard in the bylaw, though the existing cottage has a 20 meter setback and it's proposed that that setback be maintained going forward with the new development, which is consistent with the standard approach put out in the official plan and by conservation authorities. The, it's clear the new dwelling will have a larger footprint than the existing cottage. However, as I indicated, a large part of that is related to the attached garage and that attached garage is behind the house towards Old Orchard Lane and they wish to encroach into the 7.5 front yard or rear yard setback to 3.2 meters. What's interesting is it, Chair, is if the garage was detached and not part of the house, it could be as close as one meter to that rear yard. So in actual fact, having it attached to the dwelling keeps it further away from Old Orchard Lane than what the bylaw would permit if it was detached. And as a result, I'm not concerned about the reduction in the rear yard setback at all. The increased lot coverage, I think is typical of small lots that are being redeveloped. It's not an outrageous variance from the 10% to the 14%. And I believe one of the improvements is that there's a new septic system on the property as well. And that's appropriate. In general, it's our position that the proposed variance maintains the intent and purpose of what's being, trying to be achieved with the zoning bylaw. Is it a desirable and appropriate use of the land? And in our opinion, the improvement of the quality of the development, the increased energy efficiency, confirmation of a working septic system are all desirable, particularly given the waterfront nature of the property. And finally, is it minor in nature? And we feel that the impact on the surrounding neighborhood will be minor. There's already been a history of development on the property. This is going to improve the quality of development and set a standard for the area. And we feel that there will be no impacts on the surrounding neighborhood as a result of this application. Mr. Chair, my report has concluded that the four tests for the minor variance have been satisfied. My recommendation to you this evening, sir, is to look upon the application favorably. It is worth noting, although it's not a condition that's being recommended, it is standard practice that the development will have to proceed through site plan control as well as the minor variance process, but that's just matter of standard practice and doesn't require a condition. We're not recommending any conditions with this application, sir. That concludes my report. If you have any questions, I'm more than happy to attempt to address them.
